scope: Official sources for general U.S. federal and California rules, public historical economic episodes, and agency guidance. This ledger does not validate any private property value, title, rent, bill, quote, occupancy history, or forecast.

sources.title: Estate tax
sources.checked: Opened on the publisher's official domain on 2026-11-12.
sources.supports: Federal gross-estate accounting uses fair market value; the 2026 filing-threshold table; certain deductions; and the surviving-spouse portability election on a timely filed estate return.
sources.limits: A filing threshold is not a complete tax calculation. Prior taxable gifts, deductions, elections, ownership and other rules can change the result.

sources.title: What's new — Estate and gift tax
sources.checked: Opened on the publisher's official domain on 2026-11-12.
sources.supports: The IRS identifies Public Law 119-21 as setting the 2026 federal basic estate-tax exclusion at $15,000,000 and lists current estate-and-gift-tax updates.
sources.limits: The 2026 amount is year-specific and is not a forecast of later law.

sources.title: Tax inflation adjustments for tax year 2027
sources.checked: Opened on the publisher's official domain on 2026-11-12.
sources.supports: For 2027 deaths, the federal basic estate-tax exclusion is $15,480,000; the annual gift exclusion is $20,000 per recipient.
sources.limits: These are indexed statutory amounts, not a forecast for any later year.

sources.title: Gifts and inheritances: inherited property basis and sale
sources.checked: Opened on the publisher's official domain on 2026-11-12.
sources.supports: Inherited-property basis is generally fair market value at the decedent's date of death; an alternate valuation date requires an estate return and election; gain may be taxable; certain basis reporting must be consistent with final estate-tax values.
sources.limits: The FAQ describes general federal rules and exceptions. It cannot establish the basis of a specific asset.

sources.title: Instructions for Form 706
sources.checked: Opened the current July 2026 instructions on 2026-11-12; reviewed the filing-deadline and portability sections.
sources.supports: The executor's Form 706 reporting, filing and payment instructions, including the general nine-month deadline and portability election requirements.
sources.limits: The applicable filing requirement and any extension or election depend on the facts and current instructions.

sources.title: Publication 527: Residential Rental Property
sources.checked: Opened the 2025 publication on 2026-11-12; reviewed the rental-income and rental-expense sections in the current IRS text.
sources.supports: Rental income reporting and common rental expenses, including maintenance, insurance, taxes, management, repairs and utilities; personal use and improvement-versus-repair distinctions.
sources.limits: Tax treatment depends on use, ownership, records and applicable limitations. This publication does not estimate operating costs.

sources.title: Publication 559: Survivors, Executors, and Administrators
sources.checked: Opened the 2025 IRS publication page and its contents on 2026-11-12; used as a general administration checklist reference.
sources.supports: General federal tax administration for decedents, personal representatives, estates and beneficiaries.
sources.limits: A checklist, not individualized tax or legal advice; no specific filing rule is attributed to this reference in the guide.

sources.title: Retirement topics: beneficiary
sources.checked: Opened on the publisher's official domain on 2026-11-12; reviewed the current beneficiary distribution sections.
sources.supports: For deaths in 2020 or later, a designated beneficiary who is not an eligible designated beneficiary generally follows a 10-year distribution rule; eligible designated beneficiaries and spouses can have different options. Taxable distributions generally enter the recipient's gross income.
sources.limits: Distribution timing depends on the owner's death date, account, beneficiary category, plan terms and current IRS rules. No account or beneficiary facts are assumed.

sources.title: 26 U.S.C. 102: gifts and inheritances (United States Code, 2022 edition)
sources.checked: Opened on the publisher's official domain on 2026-11-12; read the full section text.
sources.supports: Subsection (a) excludes the value of property acquired by gift, bequest, devise or inheritance from gross income; subsection (b) does not exclude income generated by that property.
sources.limits: This is a general federal income-tax rule; it does not decide estate tax, inherited basis, sale gain, state tax or the treatment of a particular estate or trust. Confirm current law and facts.

sources.title: Gifts and inheritance
sources.checked: Opened on the publisher's official domain on 2026-11-12.
sources.supports: California does not include the gift or inheritance itself in the recipient's income; later income produced by inherited property may be taxable.
sources.limits: A particular sale, rental, trust or beneficiary may have additional reporting rules.

sources.title: California estate tax
sources.checked: Opened on the publisher's official domain on 2026-11-12.
sources.supports: The Controller states that a California estate-tax return is not required for decedents dying on or after January 1, 2005.
sources.limits: This does not remove federal filing obligations or other state tax questions.

sources.title: Revenue and Taxation Code section 63.2
sources.checked: Opened the current statute on the publisher's official domain on 2026-11-12.
sources.supports: California's intergenerational family-home/farm exclusion, eligibility definitions, transferee occupancy and exemption requirements, filing periods, and specified disaster-related provisions.
sources.limits: Eligibility depends on relationship, property type, use, value, timing, claims and exceptions. Obtain assessor-specific guidance.

sources.title: Proposition 19 overview and comparison charts
sources.checked: Opened on the publisher's official domain on 2026-11-12.
sources.supports: The Board's overview of intergenerational exclusions, qualifying principal residences, filing periods and the biennially adjusted value cap.
sources.limits: The Board describes the page as general summary information; the statute and assessor's determination control.

sources.title: Letter to Assessors 2025/009: intergenerational transfer value-cap adjustment
sources.checked: Opened on the publisher's official domain on 2026-11-12.
sources.supports: The statutory amount in the Proposition 19 family-home/farm value cap is adjusted every other year; the next adjustment after the 2025–2027 period is scheduled for February 2027.
sources.limits: Do not use an old rounded amount for an eligibility decision; check the current Board letter and the statute.

sources.title: Letter to Assessors 2026/026: Proposition 19 intergenerational transfer FAQs
sources.checked: Opened on the publisher's official domain on 2026-11-12; occupancy and filing sections reviewed.
sources.supports: Current Board guidance on family-home definitions, one-year occupancy, continued eligibility and claim-filing rules.
sources.limits: Fact-specific assessor guidance; not a substitute for the controlling statute or a property-specific determination.

sources.title: California Property Tax: An Overview, Publication 29
sources.checked: Opened on the publisher's official domain on 2026-11-12.
sources.supports: General California property-tax framework: a 1% base rate plus voter-approved indebtedness, change-in-ownership/new-construction reassessment rules, and the general 2% annual assessed-value limit.
sources.limits: The publication warns that law may change; the tax bill also reflects local levies and parcel-specific assessments.

sources.title: Letter to Assessors 2026/002: 2026–27 California CPI factor
sources.checked: Opened on the publisher's official domain on 2026-11-12.
sources.supports: The 2026 assessment-roll inflation factor is 1.02, reflecting the statutory 2% cap for that roll year.
sources.limits: A statewide factor does not determine a specific property's assessed value or bill.

sources.title: Revenue and Taxation Code section 480: change-in-ownership statements
sources.checked: Opened the current statute on the publisher's official domain on 2026-11-12.
sources.supports: For a real-property transfer by death outside probate, the trustee or transferee generally files a change-in-ownership statement within 150 days; for property subject to probate, the personal representative files before or with the inventory and appraisal.
sources.limits: The filing route, property scope and applicable deadlines depend on the estate and current law.

sources.title: Death of a real-property owner: reporting requirements, Publication 800-9
sources.checked: Opened on the publisher's official domain on 2026-11-12.
sources.supports: Board guidance on the death-related change-in-ownership statement, assessor notification and separate claims that may be needed for an exclusion.
sources.limits: Use the current form and directions from the assessor for the county where the property is assessed.

sources.title: Probate Code section 16061.7: trustee notification
sources.checked: Opened the current statute on the publisher's official domain on 2026-11-12.
sources.supports: Specified trust events require notice to specified beneficiaries and heirs; the statute generally sets a 60-day service period with trigger, awareness and trustee-vacancy qualifications.
sources.limits: The statute's event and recipient conditions must be checked against the actual trust and facts.

sources.title: Civil Code section 1947.12: statewide rent limits and exceptions
sources.checked: Opened the current statute on the publisher's official domain on 2026-11-12.
sources.supports: For covered units, the statewide annual rent increase ceiling is generally 5% plus the applicable cost-of-living change, or 10%, whichever is lower; exceptions and local rules matter. The statute currently states an end date of January 1, 2030.
sources.limits: Coverage and permitted increases are unit- and jurisdiction-specific; verify current law and local ordinances.

sources.title: Civil Code section 1946.2: just cause to terminate a residential tenancy
sources.checked: Opened on the publisher's official domain on 2026-11-12; reviewed the continuous-occupancy, no-fault assistance and exemption provisions.
sources.supports: After 12 months of continuous lawful occupancy, covered tenancies generally require just cause stated in the written termination notice. For a no-fault termination, the owner must either provide relocation assistance equal to one month's rent within 15 calendar days or waive the final month's rent in writing before it is due.
sources.limits: The statute lists exemptions and detailed notice conditions; occupancy history and property facts determine coverage. Local law may add protections. This summary does not establish coverage of either property or validate a specific notice.

sources.title: Revenue and Taxation Code section 11911: documentary transfer tax authorization
sources.checked: Opened the current statute on the publisher's official domain on 2026-11-12.
sources.supports: California counties and qualifying cities may impose documentary transfer taxes under local ordinance; actual local charges require the applicable ordinance and transaction facts.
sources.limits: No county or city rate is assumed in this guide.

sources.title: Listing of county assessors and tax officials
sources.checked: Opened on the publisher's official domain on 2026-11-12.
sources.supports: The Board's statewide directory lists the offices responsible for property assessment and tax administration by county.
sources.limits: This directory does not identify the jurisdiction of either property in this guide; no local assessor or contact is selected.

sources.title: SB 974 (2025–2026): status and chapter information
sources.checked: Opened the official bill-status page on 2026-11-12; it records Chapter 665, Statutes of 2026, and labels the bill non-urgency.
sources.supports: SB 974 was approved and chaptered on September 27, 2026, as Chapter 665, Statutes of 2026.
sources.limits: The status page alone does not establish the operative date or current codification; those remain unresolved here.

sources.title: Chaptered text of SB 974
sources.checked: Opened the chaptered text on the publisher's official domain on 2026-11-12; compared its section 63.2 amendment with the current code page.
sources.supports: The chaptered bill amends Revenue and Taxation Code section 63.2, including its definition of an eligible transfer medium for specified special-needs trusts.
sources.limits: The current code page reviewed here does not yet show this amendment. The guide does not treat it as a current eligibility rule; verify the operative date and codification before relying on it.

sources.title: AB 1157 (2025–2026): status
sources.checked: Opened on the publisher's official domain on 2026-11-12.
sources.supports: AB 1157, a proposal concerning tenancy and rent increases, died in the Legislature on January 31, 2026; it is not current law.
sources.limits: The status of a bill is not a prediction about future sessions.

sources.title: H.R. 1301 (119th Congress): Death Tax Repeal Act
sources.checked: Opened on Congress.gov on 2026-11-12.
sources.supports: As of the review date, H.R. 1301 is an introduced proposal referred to the House Committee on Ways and Means; it has not become law.
sources.limits: Do not apply proposed bill text to a current tax calculation. Recheck bill status before a decision.

sources.title: Compare insurance premiums
sources.checked: Opened on the publisher's official domain on 2026-11-12.
sources.supports: The Department's premium surveys are comparison tools, not individual quotes, and may omit companies or property-specific discounts and surcharges.
sources.limits: Only a current insurer quote and policy review can establish a specific premium or coverage.

sources.title: Net energy metering and net billing
sources.checked: Opened on the publisher's official domain on 2026-11-12.
sources.supports: For covered investor-owned-utility territories, export-credit and billing arrangements vary by tariff; the net-billing tariff began for new applications in 2023, while earlier net-energy-metering tariffs are closed to new enrollment.
sources.limits: A system's utility, application/interconnection date and tariff must be confirmed from its records and current bill.

sources.title: Stock Market Crash of 1929
sources.checked: Opened on the publisher's official domain on 2026-11-12.
sources.supports: The Dow Jones Industrial Average was 89% below its 1929 peak by July 1932 and did not regain its prior nominal high until 1954.
sources.limits: This is a historical equity-index episode, not a forecast or a property-specific return.

sources.title: The Great Inflation, 1965–1982
sources.checked: Opened on the publisher's official domain on 2026-11-12.
sources.supports: U.S. CPI inflation rose from a little over 1% in 1964 to more than 14% in 1980, with a peak near 15% in March 1980.
sources.limits: The historical CPI episode does not predict future inflation or the cost of a specific property.

sources.title: The Great Recession, December 2007–June 2009
sources.checked: Opened on the publisher's official domain on 2026-11-12.
sources.supports: The account reports a roughly 30% average U.S. home-price decline, a 57% S&P 500 peak-to-trough fall, and unemployment peaking at 10% in October 2009.
sources.limits: The source is a historical snapshot (some statistics are based on data available in 2013); national averages are not local property values or guaranteed future outcomes.

sources.publisher: Federal Reserve Bank of New York
sources.title: The COVID-19 pandemic and the Fed's response
sources.checked: Opened on the publisher's official domain on 2026-11-12.
sources.supports: The S&P 500 was 34% below its February 2020 high by March 23, 2020; market-wide circuit breakers halted trading three times that month.
sources.limits: This is a market stress example, not a forecast or a property-specific valuation.

sources.title: Consumer prices up 9.1% over the year ended June 2022
sources.checked: Opened on the publisher's official domain on 2026-11-12.
sources.supports: The CPI-U rose 9.1% over the twelve months ended June 2022; the same release reports a 13.7% increase in electricity prices over that period.
sources.limits: Historical national CPI categories are not a property-specific bill forecast.
